text:
noah (DevEx): Heads up — ran into a sticky install + login combo on an M1 Mac. Sharing so others don't waste cycles.

noah (DevEx): Steps: curl installer | sh (default), then `redwoodctl version` fails with `exec: "redwoodctl": executable file not found in $PATH` even though installer printed success.

noah (DevEx): I inspected: installer put binary in ~/.local/bin/redwoodctl but didn't add a symlink to /usr/local/bin. Homebrew users fine; this is for curl+sh path.

ben (Support): Do we log analytics for install method? Want to see how many use curl path.

install-bot: telemetry: install.method=script, os=macos-arm64, version=0.24.1

noah (DevEx): After fixing PATH, `redwoodctl login --profile local-test --local-serve` attempts device-code flow against local server and I hit repeated `auth: unexpected token` followed by retries. Logs: 
```
$ redwoodctl login --profile local-test --local-serve --verbose
INFO: using config /Users/noah/.redwood/config
DEBUG: profile=local-test
Launching local-serve on port 8080
INFO: opening browser to device code URL
ERROR: auth: unexpected token while parsing cached token
Authenticating... retry 1/5
ERROR: auth: unexpected token while parsing cached token
Authenticating... retry 2/5
ERROR: auth: retry limit reached
```

lina (QA): weird — what's in ~/.redwood/cache/local-test.token? could be a truncated file if installer interrupted or race with local-serve writing token.

noah (DevEx): file is 0 bytes. Repro: run `redwoodctl login --local-serve` then kill process during callback; next login sees zero-length token and crashes with parse error.

tara (Platform): This is likely two separate things: installer not ensuring `PATH` or symlink, and token write not atomic. For the token write we should use write-to-temp-and-rename pattern to avoid readers seeing partial files.

ben (Support): Also callers expect ctrl-c to abort quickly. Right now the CLI waits for retries; users hit support because they think login hung.

noah (DevEx): For local-serve specifically, might also need to lock the cache entry while the local callback writes the token to avoid simultaneous reads. On my box I saw two processes (old shell + new login) racing.

lina (QA): I'll add an e2e that: 1) runs local-serve login 2) kills process immediately after callback 3) re-runs login and asserts file is either absent or valid json (not zero bytes). Failing that, expect code to detect zero-length and remove file before retrying.

tara (Platform): Proposed fixes: 
- Installer: ensure we try creating /usr/local/bin symlink if writable; if not, print clear PATH instructions (don't silently succeed).
- Token writes: write to `cache/<profile>.token.tmp` then atomic rename to `<profile>.token` and fsync.
- On startup, treat zero-byte or non-JSON token as invalid: delete and retry immediately instead of entering the long retry loop.
- Improve retry UX: show progress `Authenticating... (retry 2/5)` and make signal handling abort faster.

noah (DevEx): +1 on better installer messaging. I wasted 10 minutes before realising my shell didn't include ~/.local/bin. The script prints a success message that felt inaccurate.

ben (Support): Could we detect common shells and give tailored PATH hints? e.g., fish vs bash vs zsh vs rc files. Even a single extra line `add "export PATH=~/.local/bin:$PATH" to your shell rc` would save time.

tara (Platform): We'll implement the token atomic write change and the installer PATH check. I'll open a draft PR and include a small migration step: on startup, if a zero-byte token is detected, delete it and log a one-off message pointing users to run login again.

install-bot: new ticket created: INSTALL-432 "installer success message but missing symlink on macOS arm64"

noah (DevEx): thanks — assigned to @tara. For immediate workaround: add ~/.local/bin to PATH or install via `brew install redwoodctl` if on mac.

lina (QA): Once PR lands I'll run regression on mac/linux and add flaky test that simulates abrupt kill during callback.

ben (Support): capturing this thread into a KB article: "redwoodctl install troubleshooting" with the two common fixes (PATH, zero-byte token).

noah (DevEx): Great. Ending note — can we also make `redwoodctl login --local-serve --output debug` spit the device_code URL so headless users can paste it manually? Some CI runners can't open browsers.

tara (Platform): Good suggestion. We'll add a `--no-browser` / `--print-url` flag and improve headless flow.
